CVE-2026-62335.title: OpenVM's OpenVmHalo2Verifier accepts non-canonical app commitments
CVE-2026-62335.description: OpenVM is a performant and modular zkVM framework built for customization and extensibility. Before 1.7.0 in the 1.x line and in affected 2.0 and 2.1 prereleases, `OpenVmHalo2Verifier.verify` accepts `appExeCommit` and `appVmCommit` as `bytes32` values without checking that either is less than the `BN254` scalar field modulus. Although public-value and proof-data lengths are checked, callers can provide non-canonical 256-bit encodings greater than or equal to that modulus at the Solidity wrapper boundary. Applications relying on the wrapper can therefore accept non-canonical app executable and app VM commitments, creating ambiguity between the supplied byte-level values and the field elements used by the verifier. This issue is fixed in versions 1.7.0, 2.0.0-rc.3 and 2.1.0-preview.

CVE-2026-99445.title: power: supply: pf1550: drain IRQ work before unregistering supplies
CVE-2026-99445.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

power: supply: pf1550: drain IRQ work before unregistering supplies

The VBUS work calls power_supply_changed(), but its managed
cancellation is registered before the supplies. Cleanup can therefore
unregister a supply while IRQ-triggered work is still pending.

Commit 838767f50747 ("power: supply: pf1550: Fix use-after-free in
power_supply_changed()") moved IRQ requests after supply registration,
but left work cancellation before the supplies. That change protects
the direct IRQ callbacks, while this fix drains the work they queue.

Register the three work items after both supplies and before the IRQs.
Cleanup then frees the IRQ producers, drains the work, and unregisters
the supplies.

The teardown ordering issue was found by static analysis.

CVE-2026-99539.title: ksmbd: fix session reference leak on compounded SESSION_SETUP
CVE-2026-99539.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix session reference leak on compounded SESSION_SETUP

A compound request can place SESSION_SETUP after another command. That
earlier command leaves a reference to its session in work->sess.
smb2_sess_setup() then overwrites work->sess with the session it looks up
or creates, and the dispatcher later puts work->sess only once. The
inherited reference is never dropped. That leaks the session, together
with its setup connection and socket, and every repeat of the compound
leaks another.

unreferenced object (size 512):
__kmalloc_cache_noprof+0x32c/0x3a0
ksmbd_smb2_session_create+0xf6/0x9c0 [ksmbd]
smb2_sess_setup+0xda4/0x6280 [ksmbd]
handle_ksmbd_work+0x88c/0x1cb0 [ksmbd]

Save the inherited session on entry. After the request has been
processed, release it once, but only when smb2_sess_setup() has replaced
work->sess with its own session or cleared it. Do this after
ksmbd_conn_unlock() so the put does not run…

CVE-2026-99621.title: drm/amdgpu: unlock the VM and BO when attaching a KFD BO fails
CVE-2026-99621.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: unlock the VM and BO when attaching a KFD BO fails

kfd_mem_attach() locks the page directory and the BO with a drm_exec
transaction on its stack, but leaves through the unwind label without
drm_exec_fini() when locking fails, e.g. when MAP_MEMORY_TO_GPU gets a
signal while the page directory or the BO is busy. Reservations already
acquired then remain locked with their ww_acquire_ctx pointing into the
expired stack frame.

With one thread doing GEM_VA map/unmap on the KFD VM and
another one mapping KFD BOs while getting SIGUSR1 every 20 us:

BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in __ww_mutex_lock.constprop.0+0x34f5/0x3da0
ww_mutex_lock_interruptible+0x2f/0x150
drm_exec_lock_obj+0x107/0x2d0 [drm_exec]
kfd_mem_attach+0x4dd/0x1b60 [amdgpu]

and the process ends up in D state.

Finish the transaction before unwinding.

(cherry picked from commit 7b885fa27e4b9fa5cbdc64e66fc35872aee296f5)

CVE-2026-99768.title: wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()
CVE-2026-99768.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()

The commit 592234e941f1 ("wifi: mac80211: Fix iTXQ AMPDU fragmentation
handling") changed the way handling of the IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag
is done in mac80211, so the only place it is set is in
ieee80211_tx_dequeue().

This means that any frames that are sent to the driver via drv_tx() will
no longer have the flag set. In particular, this affects packets going
through ieee80211_tx_pending(). Evan reported that this can result in
the ath9k driver failing to account such packets in its block ack
window, eventually overrunning the window and stalling TX.

Fix this by reinstating the flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg() when inside
a valid block ack window. This should be harmless for the TXQ path, and
will reinstate the previous behaviour for drivers that use the flag as a
signal to track the packet in the window.
